stem: Best guess: an NFP's board votes to set aside $1 million of unrestricted cash as a 'board-designated endowment.' How are those net assets classified?

choices.text: With donor restrictions — perpetual
choices.explanation: Only donors create donor restrictions.

choices.text: With donor restrictions — purpose
choices.explanation: The board, not a donor, made the designation.

choices.text: Without donor restrictions
choices.explanation: Correct. Board designations are internal and reversible.

choices.text: As a liability until spent
choices.explanation: A designation creates no obligation to an outside party.

explanation: Board-designated amounts remain net assets **without donor restrictions**; they may be disclosed or shown separately within that class.

stem: A donor gave $80,000 restricted to research. During the year the NFP spent $30,000 on research. How is the $30,000 reported?

choices.text: As an expense in net assets with donor restrictions
choices.explanation: Expenses are always reported in net assets without donor restrictions.

choices.text: No entry until the full $80,000 has been spent
choices.explanation: Releases occur as the purpose is fulfilled.

choices.text: As a reduction of the contribution revenue
choices.explanation: Revenue was properly recognized when the gift was received.

choices.text: A $30,000 release and research expense without restrictions
choices.explanation: Correct. The restriction is satisfied and the expense is unrestricted.

explanation: Reclassify $30,000 from with to without donor restrictions (net assets released), and report the $30,000 research expense in the without-donor-restrictions column.

stem: Which statement is required for all NFPs but has no direct counterpart for business entities?

choices.text: Analysis of expenses by function and nature
choices.explanation: Correct. All NFPs must present it (as a statement, on the face, or in notes).

choices.text: Statement of cash flows
choices.explanation: Businesses present one too.

choices.text: Statement of comprehensive income
choices.explanation: NFPs do not present OCI in that format.

choices.text: Statement of changes in stockholders' equity
choices.explanation: NFPs have no stockholders.

explanation: ASU 2016-14 requires every NFP to provide an analysis of expenses by both functional and natural classification.

stem: Which item is reported as a change in net assets **with** donor restrictions?

choices.text: A cash gift the donor stipulated must be used next year
choices.explanation: Correct. A time restriction makes it with donor restrictions until next year.

choices.text: Salaries of program staff
choices.explanation: Expenses are reported only in net assets without donor restrictions.

choices.text: Board-designated funds for a future building
choices.explanation: Board designations are without donor restrictions.

choices.text: Unrestricted membership dues
choices.explanation: Unrestricted revenue is without donor restrictions.

explanation: Donor-imposed time or purpose restrictions create net assets with donor restrictions. Expenses and board designations never do.

stem: An NFP received $500,000 in cash restricted by the donor to construct a building. The building was completed and placed in service this year at a cost of $500,000. Absent other stipulations, when is the restriction released?

choices.text: When the cash is received
choices.explanation: The purpose has not yet been met at receipt.

choices.text: Over the building's useful life as it is depreciated
choices.explanation: Absent a donor stipulation, the release occurs when placed in service, not over the life.

choices.text: When the building is placed in service
choices.explanation: Correct. That satisfies the purpose restriction.

choices.text: Never — building gifts are perpetually restricted
choices.explanation: Only endowment-type stipulations are perpetual.

explanation: Gifts restricted to acquire long-lived assets are released when the asset is placed in service, unless the donor stipulates how long the asset must be used.

stem: During the year an NFP had: unrestricted contributions $700,000; restricted contributions $200,000; releases from restriction $150,000; total expenses $820,000. What is the change in net assets **without** donor restrictions?

choices.explanation: This omits the releases, which increase unrestricted net assets.
This includes restricted contributions.
This includes restricted contributions and omits releases (900,000 − 820,000).

explanation: Without donor restrictions: 700,000 + releases 150,000 − expenses 820,000 = **+30,000**. (With donor restrictions: 200,000 − 150,000 = +50,000.)

stem: Which expense is classified as a **supporting activity** in an NFP's statement of activities?

choices.text: Cost of meals served at a homeless shelter
choices.explanation: Direct mission activity — a program service.

choices.text: Salary of the NFP's controller
choices.explanation: Correct. Accounting is management and general — a supporting activity.

choices.text: Scholarships awarded by an education foundation
choices.explanation: Awarding scholarships is the mission — program services.

choices.text: Vaccines administered at a free clinic
choices.explanation: Direct program service.

explanation: Supporting activities are management and general (administration, accounting, governance) and fundraising. Mission-delivery costs are program services.

stem: How must an NFP report investment return in its statement of activities?

choices.text: Gross, with investment expenses shown as management and general
choices.explanation: ASU 2016-14 requires netting external and direct internal investment expenses.

choices.text: Net of external and direct internal investment expenses
choices.explanation: Correct. Investment return is presented net of external and direct internal investment expenses; disclosure of those netted expenses is no longer required.

choices.text: Only realized gains; unrealized gains go to a separate equity account
choices.explanation: NFPs report realized and unrealized gains in the statement of activities.

choices.text: Only as a note disclosure
choices.explanation: Investment return is reported in the statement of activities.

explanation: Investment return is presented net of external and direct internal investment expenses; disclosure of those netted expenses is no longer required.

stem: An NFP's statement of financial position shows cash $300,000; receivables due in 6 months $120,000; investments $900,000 of which $600,000 is perpetual endowment corpus; and a pledge receivable restricted to next year's program $80,000. Ignoring expected releases, what financial assets are available for general expenditures within one year?

choices.explanation: Correct. 300,000 + 120,000 + (900,000 − 600,000) = 720,000; the restricted pledge is excluded.
This includes the endowment corpus and the restricted pledge.
This includes the restricted pledge.
This excludes all investments, including $300,000 that are not restricted.

explanation: Available = cash 300,000 + current receivables 120,000 + unrestricted investments 300,000 = **720,000**. Perpetually restricted corpus and purpose-restricted pledges are excluded.

stem: An NFP using the direct method in its statement of cash flows:

choices.text: Must also present the indirect-method reconciliation
choices.explanation: ASU 2016-14 removed this requirement for NFPs.

choices.text: Must present operating cash flows by net asset class
choices.explanation: Cash flows are not presented by net asset class.

choices.text: Is not required to present the indirect-method reconciliation
choices.explanation: Correct. NFPs may use the direct or indirect method; if direct, the reconciliation of change in net assets to operating cash flows is not required (ASU 2016-14).

choices.text: May omit financing activities
choices.explanation: All three categories are required.

explanation: NFPs may use the direct or indirect method; if direct, the reconciliation of change in net assets to operating cash flows is not required (ASU 2016-14).

stem: Which classification describes a donor's gift of $1,000,000 that must be invested forever, with income available for any purpose?

choices.text: Without donor restrictions, because the income is unrestricted
choices.explanation: The corpus is restricted in perpetuity.

choices.text: With donor restrictions (perpetual in nature)
choices.explanation: Correct. The corpus is a perpetual donor restriction; income, when appropriated, is without restrictions.

choices.text: Board-designated endowment
choices.explanation: The donor, not the board, imposed the restriction.

choices.text: A liability to the donor
choices.explanation: An unconditional gift is revenue, not a liability.

explanation: Donor-restricted endowment corpus is reported in net assets with donor restrictions. Earnings are reported with donor restrictions until appropriated for expenditure (per state law, e.g., UPMIFA), then released.

stem: An NFP spent $40,000 of unrestricted resources on a youth program for which it also holds a $25,000 donor-restricted gift for the same program. Absent donor instructions, how much is released from restriction?

choices.text: $0 — the NFP used unrestricted money
choices.explanation: When an expense meets a restriction, the restriction is considered satisfied even if unrestricted resources were used first.
This subtracts the gift from the spending; the release equals the restricted amount satisfied.
Correct. Qualifying expenses of $40,000 fully satisfy the $25,000 restriction.
Only $25,000 was restricted.

explanation: If an expense is incurred for a purpose for which both restricted and unrestricted resources are available, the donor restriction is treated as fulfilled to the extent of the expense. Release = lesser of the restriction (25,000) and qualifying expense (40,000).

stem: Which is **not** a required financial statement (or equivalent presentation) for a private NFP?

choices.text: Statement of activities
choices.explanation: This is one of the required NFP presentations, so it is not the answer.

choices.text: Statement of changes in fund balances by fund
choices.explanation: Correct. That is a governmental concept; NFPs report by net asset class, not funds.

choices.text: Statement of financial position
choices.explanation: This is one of the required NFP presentations, so it is not the answer.

choices.text: Statement of cash flows
choices.explanation: This is one of the required NFP presentations, so it is not the answer.

explanation: Required NFP presentations: statement of financial position, statement of activities, statement of cash flows, and the analysis of expenses by function and nature. Fund-based statements belong to governments.
